en: When both the Senate and the House of Representatives approve a bill, the President signs it to make it an official law.
If the Supreme Court finds that a new law violates the Constitution, the justices declare it unconstitutional, effectively canceling the law.
By tearing their cedula tax certificates at Pugad Lawin, Andres Bonifacio and the Katipuneros caused the official start of the Philippine revolution.
Dr. Fe del Mundo designed a bamboo incubator that uses hot water bottles to keep premature babies warm when hospital electricity fails.
The Ifugao people carved stepped rice terraces into mountains so that rainwater flows slowly down each level, preventing soil erosion and landslides.
The Commission on Elections provides private voting booths so that citizens can shade their ballots secretly, preventing others from seeing their choices.
When neighbors have a minor dispute, the barangay captain calls a mediation session to help both parties reach a peaceful agreement without court.
The national language commission chose Tagalog as the base, which evolved into modern Filipino by absorbing vocabulary from other Philippine regional languages.
After drafting the 1987 Constitution, the government held a national plebiscite where millions of voters approved the document to make it supreme law.
Devotees created the two-steps-forward, one-step-back Sinulog dance to mimic the river's current, originally performing it to honor the Santo Niño statue.
Dr. Julian Banzon extracted oil from coconuts to develop a local alternative fuel, reducing the country's reliance on imported petroleum products.
When the Philippines is in a state of war, citizens flip the national flag so the red stripe appears on top.
